title: Happy Gilmore
tagline: Hockey swing. Golf course. Good feed.
about: A failed hockey player discovers he can hit a golf ball a mile and joins the pro tour to save his grandma's house.
cue: Serve the beer when Happy pictures his perfect daydream on the green.

    StartersChubbs's golf ball cheese ballsCheddar and cream cheese balls rolled in toasted pecansHow to make it250g cream cheese150g cheddar1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce2 spring onions100g pecansBeat the cream cheese with grated cheddar, Worcestershire sauce and chopped spring onions.Roll into golf ball sizes and chill.Toast and crush the pecans, roll the balls in them and spear each with a toothpick.Grandma's biscuitsFluffy buttermilk biscuits served warm with butter and honeyHow to make it140g butter300g plain flour3 tsp baking powder1 pinch salt250ml buttermilkhoney, to serveRub the cold butter into the flour, baking powder and salt.Stir in the buttermilk, fold the dough over itself a few times and cut into rounds.Bake at 220°C.Serve warm with butter and honey.Hockey puck cheeseburger slidersHappy's first love, ice hockeyHow to make itAs written, serves 4Thick little chuck patties seared hard, cheddar melted on, in soft slider buns with pickles, onion and a smoky burger sauce.Shape 600g chuck mince into 8 thick rounds like pucks and season well.Sear in a very hot pan for 3 minutes a side, lay a half slice of cheddar on each and cover for 1 minute to melt.Mix 3 tbsp mayo, 1 tbsp tomato sauce and a pinch of smoked paprika.Toast 8 slider buns and fill with the patties, sauce, sliced pickles and thin onion.Bacon and egg breakfast muffinsNot what Shooter eats for breakfast.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsGrandma's meatloafBeef and pork meatloaf with a tomato glaze, mash and peasHow to make it80g breadcrumbs100ml full cream milk500g beef mince250g pork mince1 brown onion1 egg4 tbsp tomato sauce1 tbsp brown sugar1kg potatoes300g frozen peasSoak the breadcrumbs in the milk. Grate the onion.Mix lightly with the beef and pork mince and egg, and press into a loaf tin.Glaze with the tomato sauce mixed with the sugar and bake at 180°C.Peel and boil the potatoes and mash. Cook the peas.Sponsor's sweet onion chicken footlongHappy's Subway deal. Teriyaki chicken, salad, sweet onion sauceHow to make it600g chicken thigh fillets80ml teriyaki sauce2 long crusty rolls4 slices of Swiss cheese2 cos lettuce leaves, shredded2 tomatoes, sliced1/2 red onion, finely sliced3 tbsp mayonnaise2 tbsp sweet chilli sauce1 tbsp honey1 tsp white vinegarToss the chicken in half the teriyaki and leave while you slice the salad.Mix the mayonnaise, sweet chilli, honey and vinegar for the sweet onion sauce.Grill the chicken until charred and cooked through, brushing with the rest of the teriyaki. Slice.Split and toast the rolls with the cheese inside, fill with the chicken and salad, drizzle with sauce and cut each into two.SweetsGrandma's lemon barsShortbread base with tart lemon filling, dusted with icing sugarHow to make it240g plain flour80g icing sugar150g soft butter4 eggs300g caster sugar150ml lemon juice4 lemonsPress most of the flour, 60g of the icing sugar and the butter into a lined 20cm tin.Bake the base at 170°C.Whisk the eggs, caster sugar, remaining flour, lemon juice and zest of two lemons, and pour over the hot base.Bake until just set.Cool, dust with the remaining icing sugar and cut into bars.DrinksHappy's lemon shandy pitchersLager and lemon soda over lemon wheels, served by the pitcherHow to make it2 L lager4 lemons60ml sugar syrup500ml soda waterChill two big jugs in the freezer.Stir the juice of three lemons with the sugar syrup and soda water.Pour half the lager into each jug down the side, then top each with half the lemon soda.Add lemon wheels and pour into chilled glasses.Cold chocolate milkFrom Grandma's kitchen, no IRS letters attached.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
